member.name: T:Plasma.ConsoleCommandAttribute
member.summary: Exposes a static method as a console command, callable from the engine's console.
member.remarks: The method must be static. Parameters are limited to bool, int, uint, float, double and string, because the console's command interpreter is Lua and marshals through plVariant; anything else is a compile error rather than a surprise at the prompt. A return value is allowed but ignored, matching native console functions.

example.code: [ConsoleCommand("ai.reveal", "(bool enabled) - draw every agent's current path")] public static void Reveal(bool enabled) => AiDebug.DrawPaths = enabled;

member.name: T:Plasma.ConsoleTool
member.summary: A debug panel drawn by the engine console. Derive from this, mark it with , and draw with in .

remarks.para: One instance is created per script generation and lives until that generation is unloaded, so a tool may hold state across frames - but not across a script rebuild.

runs on the engine's main thread inside the console's ImGui frame, between a Begin/End pair the console owns. Calling ImGui from anywhere else is outside a frame and will fail. If the method throws, or leaves ImGui's stacks unbalanced, the console disables the tool rather than letting it corrupt the rest of the UI.

member.name: T:Plasma.DebugDraw
member.summary: Debug rendering. Everything draws into the world of the script that is currently executing and lasts one frame, except the AddPersistent* calls, which last for a given duration.

remarks.para: These call the engine through a fixed function table: no boxing, no argument arrays, nothing allocated per call. That matters because debug drawing is the API most likely to be called inside a loop - and for real loops, submits a whole batch in one crossing.

This sits beside the generated Debug class rather than replacing it. Debug exposes 13 of plDebugRenderer's entry points through the reflected binding path, which allocates roughly six times per call; DebugDraw covers the whole surface and allocates nothing. Existing Debug.* calls keep working unchanged.
